findings.title: Unauthenticated full user-object exposure on /rest/memories (password hashes, deluxeToken, totpSecret)
findings.analysis: GET /rest/memories returns HTTP 200 with all 10 memory records, each embedding a full User object (UserId, id, username, email, 32-hex password hash, role, deluxeToken, lastLoginIp, profileImage, totpSecret, isActive, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt). Observed 2026-10-05T04:17Z: status 200, 6183 bytes, Content-Type application/json. Example user: email bjoern@owasp.org, password hash 9283f1b2e9669749081963be0462e9466, role deluxe, deluxeToken efe2f1599e2d93440d5243a1ffaf5a413b70cf3ac97156bd6fab9b5ddfcbe0e4, totpSecret (empty string). UserIds 1,4,13,18,19 mapped to emails including bjoern@owasp.org, bjoern.kimminich@gmail.com, ethereum@juice-sh.op, john@juice-sh.op, emma@juice-sh.op. Null case: /rest/wallet/balance, /rest/basket, /rest/user/authentication-details, /api/SecurityAnswers/ all return 401 without auth. Control: Authorization: Bearer fake-jwt-token returns IDENTICAL 200/6183 (no header in signature), proving the exposure is not session-dependent but route-specific. This matches the app's Password Hash Leak challenge family (id=1, 'Obtain the password (hash) of the currently logged-in user directly from a REST API endpoint').
findings.false_positive_check: The 6183-byte response with all user objects reproduces on a fresh request and is stable across scrapes (same size/ETag). The control endpoints require auth (401), so the leak is endpoint-specific, not a global misconfiguration. The leaked deluxeToken is not a valid signed JWT (no header in signature), reducing session-hijack value but not the sensitive-data exposure. No benign alternative explains an unauth GET leaking password hashes and totpSecrets for all users.

findings.title: Unauthenticated POST write gap on /api/SecurityAnswers/ (read path gated, write path accepts unauth insertions)
findings.analysis: Read path is auth-gated: GET /api/SecurityAnswers/ returns 401 without Authorization. Write path is open: POST /api/SecurityAnswers/ with an empty JSON body and NO Authorization header returns 201 with Location /api/SecurityAnswers/24 and JSON body {"status":"success","data":{"id":24,"answer":null,"SecurityQuestionId":null,"UserId":null,...}}. Sending the identical request again returns 201 with a NEW id (id:25 on this boot; monotonic server-side increment), proving unauthenticated server-side persistence with no ownership, validation, or dedup checks. Empty-object POST also yields 201. Neighboring write endpoints correctly gate or fail: /api/Complaints/ 401, /api/Cards/ 401, /api/Addresses/ /Reviews/ /Questions/ /Memberships/ /Coupons/ /RecoveryAnswers/ /UserAccounts/ /ProductLabels/ all return 500 'Unexpected path' (wrapped). This is a classic read-vs-write differential authorization gap: the same route reads 401 but writes 201 without any credentials.
findings.false_positive_check: Verified with two independent identical POSTs on fresh requests; each yields a distinct server-assigned id (24 then 25 on 2026-10-05T04:17Z boot), confirming real insertions rather than a mock 201. No Authorization header present in either request. CORS Origin does not block. Neighbors gate correctly, so this is a per-endpoint gap, not broken auth globally. The null UserId/answer fields confirm no authentication context is attached.

findings.title: SQL filter bypass on /rest/products/search?q= via tautology (unfiltered catalog disclosure)
findings.analysis: GET /rest/products/search?q=Apple returns 200/921 bytes (3 products: ids 1, 24, 47) while GET /rest/products/search?q=%27%20OR%20%271%27=%271 returns 200/16557 bytes with the COMPLETE 46-product catalog. The tautology occurs in 0 of 46 product names yet returns all rows, proving the filter parameter is not safely handled. Malformed input (UNION) returns a 30-byte error response, and earlier variants showed raw SQLITE_ERROR 500 for truly malformed payloads — input reaches the query layer. Deduced predicate: WHERE name LIKE '%' || <q> || '%'. Catalog disclosure is the confirmed impact; deterministic credential/data extraction channels (AND-branch contradiction / UNION column extraction) were probed and are unproven/unclaimed in this variant.
findings.false_positive_check: Differential pair reproduced fresh at 2026-10-05T04:17Z: q=Apple -> 921 B (3 products), q=tautology -> 16557 B (all 46). The 921-byte filtered response is the expected benign null case; the 16557-byte response demonstrably exceeds the legitimate result set. Pagination/order params (orderBy/limit/skip/where) were tested and ignored (full catalog returned regardless), consistent with the same unsafely-constructed filter. Byte size 16557 stable across scrapes. Extraction-channel unclaiming is intentional; the confirmed finding is filter bypass + full catalog disclosure.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Prometheus-style observability surface on /metrics
findings.analysis: GET /metrics (no Authorization) returns HTTP 200 text/plain version=0.0.4, ~26111 bytes, containing operational telemetry gauges: juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total/output_tokens/llm_tool_calls_total, http_requests_count (by status), juiceshop_startup_duration_seconds. The pinned v20.2.0 base image serves no /metrics endpoint, so this surface is mutation-introduced. A secrets scan of all counter lines against the patterns secret/password/token/key/credential/api_key/bearer/x-api found only HELP-text hits on generic word 'token'; no emitted secrets or credentials.
findings.false_positive_check: Verified fresh at 2026-10-05T04:17Z: 200/text/plain/version=0.0.4/26111 B without any Authorization header. Stable across scrapes. The baseline v20.2.0 does not serve /metrics, establishing the surface as mutation-introduced rather than baseline Juice Shop behavior. No secrets in output; impact is operational telemetry disclosure (LLM usage, startup duration, request counts by status), rated Low relative to the disclosure/write-gap findings.

findings.title: Unauthenticated per-user security-question disclosure and account existence enumeration via /rest/user/security-question?email=
findings.analysis: GET /rest/user/security-question?email=<email> is reachable without authentication. For existing users with a configured security question it returns 200 + a JSON object embedding the question text: bjoern@owasp.org -> {"question":{"id":7,"question":"Name of your favorite pet?",...}}; emma@juice-sh.op -> id=10 "Company you first work for as an adult?"; john@juice-sh.op -> id=14 "What's your favorite place to go hiking?". For users without a configured question or nonexistent addresses it returns 200 + an empty object {}. Observed 2026-10-05T04:17Z: bjoern@owasp.org -> 200/139 B with question; emma@juice-sh.op -> 200/153 B; john@juice-sh.op -> 200/154 B; test@nonexistent.invalid -> 200/2 B {}; admin@juice.sh -> 200/2 B {}. The differential {} vs {"question":...} constitutes an account-existence signal for users with configured questions. The question text is sensitive reset-authorization material. This maps to the Email Leak / security-question information-disclosure challenge families.
findings.false_positive_check: Reproduced on fresh requests at 2026-10-05T04:17Z with exact email-encoded parameters. The {} response is NOT a 404/500 error but a distinct 200/2 B JSON body, so the distinction is an application-level response difference, not an error path. Multiple existing users (bjoern@owasp.org, emma@juice-sh.op, john@juice-sh.op) each return their own question text, confirming per-user data exposure rather than a default/template. Control: the read path requires auth in the neighboring /rest/user/* family (e.g., /rest/user/authentication-details -> 401), so the gap is specific to security-question. The {} vs question-text differential is observable regardless of whether the {} case denotes nonexistent vs no-question users, so the core disclosure finding (per-user security question text exposed unauth) is not weakened by that ambiguity.
